# Generated byte-buffer execution contract

This pilot extends the generated-program approach beyond the scalar contract.
The sole behavior authority is model/bytes-contract.json, an IR 0.2 program.
It concatenates an existing buffer and application data, takes a prefix and a
suffix at an arbitrary integer offset, and reconstructs the entire content.
The generated equality is content equality, never merely length equality.

Semantics.v defines separate byte/integer expression sorts, total truncating
slice (Z.to_nat clamps negative offset/count independently), concatenation,
length and ordered byte assignments. The execution theorem quantifies over
all initial byte environments, byte inputs and unbounded integer offsets.
Lists of integers include all legal octets; proving the stronger list theorem
does not restrict payloads or introduce an input length bound. The generated
initial state is checked separately. The proof body is specific to this contract.

compile.py rejects unsupported semantic fields, control, guards, timers,
messages, actions and operations. A separate inverse typed constructor parser
recovers initial values, event field domains, all actions in order and all
content equalities. Additional Rocq code, omitted fields or changed expressions
are rejected. JSON/type validation, the structural bridge, denotation and
orchestration remain trusted; this is not a universal compiler/interpreter proof.
No TCP, output-order, time, network implementation or liveness theorem follows.

Run `python3 formal/rocq-bytes/check.py --docker --out <fresh-directory>`.
The fixed Rocq 9.2.0 container is the same digest as the existing scalar pilot.
The gate compiles actual generated program theorems, requires two empty-axiom
audits and independently kernel-checks three objects. Two altered source models
(wrong suffix count, wrong assignment order) must have valid generated modules
but fail the execution proof, with real reference invariant counterexamples.
A separate injected axiom must be exposed by the assumption audit.

Without Rocq/Docker the explicit result is not_run, kernel_checked_proof=false.
The seven local binding/reference methods are not kernel evidence. CI runs the
actual gate and retains sources, objects, logs, source and toolchain hashes;
its result needs provenance/byte binding acceptance before being reported as a
kernel checkpoint. Older proof epochs and their input hashes are unchanged.
